Finding Ground in an Uncertain World: Ancient Wisdom for Modern Turbulence

Inspire Me!
The world feels increasingly chaotic—from economic pressure to global political shifts and an unpredictable future. When external conditions are completely out of our hands, how do we keep from feeling overwhelmed?
This interactive workshop bridges contemporary psychology with timeless philosophy to help us build unshakeable internal resilience and stay anchored in times of uncertainty. We’ll look at the big picture, unpack what it means to live with the unknown, and share practical tools to maintain clarity amidst the noise.




Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host, Sivananda:

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

long_description:
Overview

A concert in three circles moving between installation, sound and performance.

Curated by composer-artists Elliot Vaughan and Noel Meek, STROMA transforms Massey’s Great Hall into a space for listening, wandering and encountering music from different perspectives.

The evening unfolds in three circles.

From 7:00pm, arrive at your own pace for an open, self-guided installation in the Great Hall. Wander through a collection of intimate works, sounds and performances, taking time to explore the space before gathering at 7:30pm.

At 7:30pm, the space transforms for Gordon Monahan’s Speaker Swinging, as performers set speakers into motion, sending sound and circles of light through the Great Hall.

Then, at approximately 8:00pm, the audience gathers in the round for a seated concert of chamber music, bringing together works by composers from Aotearoa and beyond, including a new commission by Eve de Castro-Robinson.

From open exploration, through sound and movement, to a concert in the round, the evening moves between different ways of listening, experiencing and inhabiting the space.

long_description:
Overview

Join us in Wellington to hear from the design and construction teams that brought this innovative project to life.

Join us on 17 November at Tonkin + Taylor for our final BIMinNZ Wellington event of 2026, as we explore the technology, innovation and collaboration behind Air New Zealand's remarkable new Hangar 4 project.

Designed by Studio Pacific Architecture and constructed by NZ Strong, Hangar 4 is the Southern Hemisphere's largest single span timber aircraft hangar. This impressive 15,000m² facility features a 98 metre clear span, enormous prefabricated timber trusses weighing 38 tonnes each, and an innovative approach to sustainable construction that sets a new benchmark for aviation infrastructure.

We'll be joined by Patrick Thompson from Studio Pacific Architecture and Jimmy Corric from NZ Strong, who will take us behind the scenes of this extraordinary project, exploring the digital tools, innovative construction methodologies and collaborative processes that helped bring it to life.

From complex design coordination and prefabrication to the challenges of construction within an operational airport environment, this session promises valuable insights into how technology and innovation are helping deliver some of New Zealand's most ambitious projects.

Come along to connect with Wellington's digital built environment community, hear from the people behind this impressive project, and celebrate another fantastic year of BIMinNZ events!

long_description:
Overview

Many of us have financial questions we've been meaning to ask for years but never get around to. This is your chance to ask them.

We're surrounded by financial information. Social media, podcasts, news articles, online calculators, investment commentary, and endless opinions from friends and family.

With so much information available, it's easy to feel overwhelmed or unsure about what's actually relevant to your situation.

That's why I'm hosting a small group discussion for people who have questions about their financial future, whatever stage of life they're at, but aren't sure where to start.

We'll explore some of the questions that keep many people awake at night:

Am I making the right financial decisions?
What happens if life doesn't go to plan?
How do I balance enjoying life now with preparing for the future?
What financial risks am I not seeing?
Will I have enough to retire comfortably?
I'm earning an income, so why does it feel so hard to get ahead?

And perhaps most importantly:

What's one financial question you've always wanted answered but never asked?

Join us for an open, relaxed conversation where no question is too simple, and the discussion is driven by what matters most to the people in the room.

long_description:
Overview

An in-person Motu Public Policy Seminar on global shifts in the labour market and what they could mean for Aotearoa New Zealand

Join us for a Motu Research (with support from The Treasury New Zealand) public policy seminar on "Global shifts in the labour market and what they could mean for Aotearoa New Zealand".

We have four speakers with expertise in labour markets (Alexander Hijzen, OECD; Dr Lisa Meehan, Director, New Zealand Policy Research Institute; Christopher Ball, RBNZ; and Amanda Reid, CEO of BERL). Their presentations will be followed by audience questions.

You can attend this seminar either in person or online. We will provide the recording and slides afterwards.

For in person participants - please allow yourself time to sign in at The Treasury reception (level 3, 1 The Terrace). Morning tea is available at the venue from 10am.

Motu Research seminars bring expert research into conversation with policy makers, researchers and other stakeholders. Speakers present their findings, then take questions from a panel and the audience. Recent seminars have covered Treasury's social discount rate, children's development, and public housing and wellbeing. You can see recordings of our past seminars here.

When: 17 November from 10.30am-12pm (if attending in person, morning tea served from 10am).

Where: The Treasury seminar room, 1 The Terrace, Wellington AND on online.


Video call details for online participants:
Microsoft Teams meeting
Join: https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/411230592011907?p=LzPaskP44f1CqcwCCU
Meeting ID: 411 230 592 011 907
Passcode: nk2hV9NW


About the speakers

Alexander Hijzen, OECD is a senior economist at the Directorate for Employment, Labour and Social Affairs of the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD), the project leader of the OECD LinkEED 2.0 network and a Research Fellow of IZA@LISER. He has previously worked at the International Monetary Fund and the Centre for Research on Globalisation and Economic Policy (GEP) at the University of Nottingham. His research has been published in international academic journals. Alexander holds a Ph.D. in Economics from the University of Nottingham and is of Dutch citizenship. He has worked on job mobility, labour reallocation, ageing and productivity. He works on income distribution and labour economics more broadly. Alexander will speak about two chapters in the recent OECD analysis called Employment Outlook. The chapters are “Reviving growth in an ageing world: The role of job mobility”, that includes Aotearoa New Zealand - and “Places and people: The impact of structural change on local labour markets”.

Dr Lisa Meehan, Director, New Zealand Policy Research Institute, Auckland University of Technology. Lisa is an applied economist with extensive experience in economic research and public policy, having previously worked at the OECD, the New Zealand Productivity Commission and the New Zealand Treasury. Her research focuses on labour markets, productivity, education, health, workforce diversity and inequality. She is particularly interested in how technological change (including artificial intelligence) may affect skills development, employment opportunities and labour market inequality. She has recently worked on productivity growth, New Zealand’s labour income share, and broader shifts in labour markets.

Christopher Ball, RBNZ is a Senior Advisor in the Research and Analytics team at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. His recent work includes research on job-to-job mobility in New Zealand and the exposure of the New Zealand labour market to artificial intelligence and robotics.

The Aura is your energetic field—the subtle electromagnetic energy that surrounds your body. A strong, balanced aura helps you feel grounded, confident, resilient, and protected, allowing you to move through life with greater vitality and ease. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll strengthen this energetic field, leaving you feeling centred, uplifted, and radiant.

long_description:
Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 06 354 5555

long_description:
Overview

Stoned-Em Sounds Summer Slam 2026 spearfishing and ocean cleanup competition

The Stoned-Em crew, in collaboration with Henderson’s, proudly presents the Stoned-Em Sounds Summer Slam 2026 Spearfishing & Ocean Clean-Up Competition!

4th–6th December 2026

New Zealand’s biggest spearfishing and ocean clean-up competition is back! This year we’ve mixed things up with a new format and new venues, while keeping the three-day competition across the Marlborough Sounds.

The competition boundaries cover a massive 4,000 km², and competitors can shore dive, kayak or use a boat.

NEW REGISTRATION & BRIEFING FORMAT

Register anytime between 9:00am–7:00pm on Friday 4th December at Henderson’s, 38 Grove Road, Mayfield, Blenheim.

At registration, you’ll sign in and watch the compulsory briefing video, covering the rules, safety information and the big reveal – the seven target species for 2026.

You’ll also collect a $15 Henderson’s voucher and 1.5 kg Fish Magnet burley, which are included with your entry.

THREE DAYS – SEVEN SPECIES

Our scoring system means the number of different species entered is more important than weight, encouraging competitors to target different species rather than simply up-sizing their catch.

It’s two divers per team and $75 per diver.

OCEAN CLEAN-UP – LET’S BREAK 10 TONNES!

Looking after the marine environment we all enjoy is a huge part of the Summer Slam.

Since the competition began, our competitors have removed approximately 7.8 tonnes of rubbish from the Marlborough Sounds. In 2026, we want your help to push that total beyond 10 tonnes!

We’re introducing new ocean rubbish categories this year, alongside some awesome prizes. Details will be revealed at the briefing.

NEW WEIGH-IN VENUE – BOOMTOWN BEER GARDEN

On Sunday 6th December, we’re taking the weigh-in and prizegiving to Boomtown Beer Garden, 19 Blicks Road, Renwick.

Weigh-in: 1:00–3:00pm. Strict 3:00pm cut-off.

We’re also turning Sunday into a family fun day, so bring your friends and family along! There’ll be food, drinks, a bucking bronco, bouncy castle, the weigh-in and prizegiving.

Proceeds from food, beverages and fundraising activities will support our 2026 charity – the Starship Foundation.

COMPETITION MERCH

Official 2026 Summer Slam merchandise can be ordered when purchasing your competition ticket, with all profits going to the Starship Foundation. So make sure you order online so you don’t miss out!

HOW TO ENTER*

Purchase your ticket – entries are limited to 300 competitors.
Register at Henderson’s between 9:00am–7:00pm Friday 4th December, watch the compulsory briefing and collect your Henderson’s voucher and burley.
Comply with the Stoned-Em Sounds Summer Slam 2026 Rules, which will be provided electronically and available at registration.
Come to Boomtown on Sunday for the 1:00–3:00pm weigh-in, followed by prizegiving.

*T&Cs apply.

After the information session, take the opportunity to connect with peers and IELTS experts over champagne, beer, wine, non-alcoholic beverages, and canapés. Attendees will also receive a certificate of attendance, which can be used to claim CPD points.




Who should attend?

This event is designed for organisations that rely on IELTS results, including:

Education Providers: International directors, Senior Admissions & Recruitment leaders, and policymakers.
Professional Associations: Registration officers and managers involved in setting or reviewing English language requirements.
Employers: HR and recruitment professionals setting proficiency standards.
Government: Policy and project officers working on admissions or migration requirements.






*This event is exclusive for organisations that rely on IELTS results for admission, entry, registration or application purposes. We have dedicated events for test takers and English language teachers.

Overview

Discover how leading organisations uncover hidden risks, prioritise investment and make better decisions with confidence.

Executive Briefing for CIOs, Strategy, Digital and Transformation Leaders



AI, transformation, cyber resilience and cost optimisation continue to dominate executive agendas, yet many organisations still lack a connected view of how these priorities impact the broader enterprise.

Join Kapish and Ardoq for an executive briefing exploring how leading organisations are making better decisions through greater visibility across strategy, business capabilities, technology, risk and investment.

Using a fictional organisation facing familiar business challenges, our consultants will walk through a series of executive scenarios involving transformation, AI adoption, technology risk, application rationalisation and operational resilience. We'll demonstrate how leaders can better understand impacts, dependencies and risk through a connected enterprise view enabled by Ardoq.

You'll gain practical insights into how organisations are:

Understanding the impact of strategic and technology decisions
Identifying hidden dependencies and risks
Reducing complexity and unnecessary duplication
Prioritising transformation and technology investments
Strengthening governance for AI and business change

The session includes practical use cases, a live demonstration of the scenarios within Ardoq, and opportunities for questions with our consultants and enterprise architecture specialists.

Lunch and refreshments provided. Places are limited.
